queue.body:
The order in which each lampOS builder takes its tasks. Kept by the first builder (the one with lamp-4ace); only it edits this body. Decided by the owner and the first builder on 2026-10-14 (`fifth-P3`), replacing the list in `lampOS/docs/work-split.md`, which keeps the rules, the loops, "What the lamp showed" and the history of finished tasks.

**A builder's next task:** the first issue in its own list below that is open and not `status:taken`. Claim it as `lampOS/docs/joining.md` says ("Tasks as GitHub issues"): add `status:taken`, comment `taken by <name> · session <id> · <lamp or none>`, then read the comments again and release it if the first "taken" comment is not yours. Questions and answers are comments on the task's issue. A proposal is a new issue labelled `proposal` and `builder:<name>`; the first builder answers it in a comment, and no answer means not allowed. A finished task is handed back as one pull request from `<name>/<task>` into `lamp-voice`, not a draft, with its ARM64 run green (joining.md, "One pull request per task", `fifth-P6`, decided 18:33); the first builder merges it after its minute on lamp-4ace, and the merge closes the issue.

Owner's order of 2026-10-14, 14:00: parts that stand on their own first, the harder ones later. And at 17:22: "reimagine the entire experience. make lamp the most fun creature to interact with": the design is `lampOS/docs/creature.md`; its pieces (#710-#714) come first. Stopping and interruption are tested by the first builder in the evenings.

## The V2 MVP first: wide, then deep (the owner, 2026-10-15 00:37)

"prioritize the tasks for builders with ruthless priority. so we have an end to end experience on lamp first. then we'll optimize each component and edge cases later … wide first. deep later … have all the pieces in place make sure the whole works. then after that, have builders optimize each component."

So until every piece below is on lamp-4ace and works with the others, a builder works only on its MVP tasks. Everything else waits under "After the MVP", even if already taken: pause it, push what you have, and say so on its issue.

| What a person gets | State on lamp-4ace (2026-10-15 00:40) | Missing piece, and whose |
|---|---|---|
| Talk to it naturally: turns, interruptions, noise | On and working | — |
| It looks alive: body, light, the eye, breathing, sleep at night | On; the eye and the night sleep not yet seen working | first builder checks |
| It sees you: turns to your face, hello when you arrive, turns to a call | On; turning to a call on since 00:57 (#724 merged) | — |
| It does things: light, volume | On | — |
| Reminders and timers by voice | **On since 04:39** (#747 merged): "set a timer for one minute" → "One minute, starting now." … "Your timer is done."; reminders set, listed, cancelled and said when due | third: a reminder "in two minutes" comes up to a minute early (follow-up on #747) |
| It remembers you, across days | **On since 02:47** (#743 merged): "what did we talk about yesterday?" answered from last night | — |
| It works for you: hands tasks to Claude Code and tells you the result | **Works end to end**: the played day at 01:25 handed a poem to Claude Code and told the result unasked 39 s later | **#736 (second)**: a yes in two breaths still lost; #740's first try failed its minute (it ended the voice whenever news was told) |
| You can touch it: button, base strip, head pads | Button on; touch merged 01:17, off until tuned with a hand | **#711 (third), first builder at the lamp today** |
| It starts by itself after power, and every part comes back | Every part enabled at boot (the eyes since 01:32) except the body, started by hand until #703; the body's wake from fold shown; a power cut not tried | **#702, then #701 (fifth)** |
| It is safe: gives way to a hand, never hurts itself | Not built | **#703 (fifth)** |
| It gets new software by itself | **Works** (#741 merged): at 03:48 lamp-4ace updated itself to build 188 from a signed test channel, every part well. Publishing waits on the owner's signing key | **#737 (second)**: the `publish:` job; the owner: the key |

How a lamp is set up (phone, desktop) is not decided by the owner and is not in the MVP yet.

The first builder plays the whole lamp end to end every evening (a person's day: arrive, talk, ask, hand over work, get news, a reminder, touch, leave, night) and files each fault as an issue to a builder with room.

### second
1. #737 — 45. Updates: `lamp-update` merged (#741) and tried on lamp-4ace; next the `publish:` job, ready for the owner's key (MVP)
2. #736 — 44. A yes said in two breaths still starts the task (MVP: the hand-over breaks without it)

After the MVP: #723 (the early end; pause it), #732 (progress news through Jev), #733 (Codex and the others), #694 (the bare name: the #725 model heard 1 of 6 calls), #714 (always alive: done unless the first builder finds the sleep broken)

### first (the first builder's own, while a builder is away)
1. #712 — 34. The eye (taken at 19:52 from the second, whose session was idle; on lamp-4ace since 20:15, waits for a person at the lamp)
2. The voice's first-output record for the judge (proposed in #722's `voice-first-output.md`): first part on lamp-4ace since 20:48 (`bf01f7e6d`); `request_outcome` waits on the fourth's answer in #700

### third
1. Follow-up to #747: a time from now ("in two minutes") goes to `set_timer`, not a rounded `set_reminder` (MVP)
2. #711 — 33. Touch: #728 merged 01:17 (its minute without `--touch` passed). Turned on with a person at the lamp today: thresholds, E4/E8, then on by default (MVP)

After the MVP: #699 — 8. A shared log, settings, and reports from the parts that give none

Done: #695 — 6 (on lamp-4ace since 16:53) · #696 — 11 (on `lamp-voice`; off on lamp-4ace until the voice uses it)

### fourth
1. #739 — 46. The voice's timed process tests fail on a loaded host (speed for every builder's gate)

Next: the faults the first builder's end-to-end runs find.

Done: #698 — 29 (pull request #743, merged 02:51; on lamp-4ace since 02:47) · #697 — 28 (on lamp-4ace since 2026-10-14 16:54) · #713 — 35 (pull request #727, merged 23:01) · #707 — 30 (pull request #721, merged; on lamp-4ace since 20:21) · #700 — 17 (pull request #722, merged)

### fifth
1. #702 — 23. Waking up after the power comes back: now the whole lamp, every part, from power (MVP)
2. #701 — 27. The keeper (MVP)
3. #703 — 24. Giving way to a hand, and not hurting itself (MVP)

After the MVP: #720 (seeing someone speak; pause it), #704 (weighing and measuring the lamp)

Done: #715 — 37 (pull request #724, merged 01:00; on lamp-4ace with `--look-at-name on` since 00:57) · #710 — 32 (pull request #718, merged; on lamp-4ace since 18:41) · #719 — 38 (pull request #726, merged 23:00; its body on lamp-4ace)

comments.body: First builder, 2026-10-14 17:38, to every builder: the ARM64 run's failure in `crates/controls/tests/program.rs` (`sigterm_finishes_recording_and_releases_the_actual_serve_owner`, `No such file or directory`) was the workflow's, not your code: the Debian 12 container lacked `/bin/kill` (procps). Fixed on `lamp-voice` (`.github/workflows/lampos-arm64.yml`); rebase onto it and the run should pass. Do not change that test for it.

First builder, 2026-10-14 18:23, to every builder: the second ARM64 failure, `crates/surround/tests/selection.rs` (`interrupted_collection_leaves_only_unaccepted_files_and_retry_removes_them`), was the workflow again: the Debian container ran the tests as root, and root ignores the read-only folder the test relies on. Fixed on `lamp-voice` (`91a0fdb3a`): the job now runs on GitHub's Ubuntu 22.04 ARM machine as an ordinary user (glibc 2.35, so its binaries run on the lamps' Debian 12). Rebase onto it; do not change that test. If a run still fails on something that passes on your Mac, say it on your task's issue and I look at the workflow first.

First builder, 19:36, to every builder: the ARM64 run is green on `lamp-voice` for the first time (run 38559471390, `21c24fc0a`: Ubuntu 22.04 on ARM64, as an ordinary user, whole workspace built and tested one test at a time). What had kept it red was the workflow (no `procps`; tests run as root) and one Records open that only fails when not root (`O_NOATIME`, mended in `21c24fc0a`). Since `652a196e1` `cargo clippy -p lamp-body --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passes on Linux. Rebase your task branches on `origin/lamp-voice`; a pull request is ready when its own run is green (joining.md, "One pull request per task"). On a Mac, run `lamp-body` and `lamp-voice` tests with `-- --test-threads=1`: some of their tests fail in parallel there.

pr-747.body:
Closes #709

Kind: off unless set.

`LAMP_SCHEDULE_TOOLS=on` exposes six Schedule tools in Voice and enables their Actions routes; both roles require the exact value `on`. `LAMP_SCHEDULE_SPEAK=on` separately enables Voice's isolated reminder consumer, with `LAMP_SCHEDULE_DELIVERY_DIR` provisioned as private persistent state. No deployment file changes.

Default-off proof: fresh `1337e7e1d8` baseline and implementation source copies passed **72 cases / 144 exact stdout comparisons**, without normalization, across two profiles and all 36 combinations of absent/non-enabling switch values. The boundary is public catalogs, declarations, existing route lists and ordinary Written requests; functional tests separately exercise real routes. All 34 local package manifests resolve inside each copy. [Raw comparisons, helper sources and copy audit](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/standalone-1337/README.md).

Verification: [task source and historical evidence](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/d794cf2aca8fd5a7891af6363f2155e9fd3091fe/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-host-20261014/README.md), [final focused checks](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/d794cf2aca8fd5a7891af6363f2155e9fd3091fe/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-host-20261014/integration-1337/README.md), and [terminal qualification index](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/README.md). Earlier failed runs retain their actual source IDs and outcomes.

Gate on Third's Intel i7-10700K x86_64 Mac, macOS 26.6.2 / Darwin 25.6.0, 64 GiB RAM, Rust/Cargo 1.96.0, from `lampOS/`:

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — passed.
- `cargo clippy --offline --locked -p lamp-actions -p lamp-schedule -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed.
- Seven documented Voice filters — **136 test executions / 0 failed / 2 ignored**. The Days exclusion test appears in two filters; these are executions, not unique tests. Exact commands are retained in the focused record.
- `cargo build --offline --locked --workspace` — passed.
- `cargo test --offline --locked -p lamp-actions -p lamp-schedule -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1` — **FAILED: 1,764 passed / 1 failed / 13 ignored**, 77 harnesses, exit 101, 2,013.072357316 seconds.
- Independent source copy: workspace/helper builds passed, **435 test executions / 0 failed / 7 ignored**, plus all 144 off-switch comparisons.
- Two existing host timing probes run explicitly once each after local builds/tests ended: **2 / 0 / 0**, 606 raw poll samples. Maximum parent poll 0.325789 ms; maximum transport poll 0.063886 ms, below the 2 ms reference. [Boundaries and samples](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/timing-1337/README.md) exclude startup, storage, providers, audio and lamp behavior; neither probe asserts a timing threshold.

The sole complete-gate failure is unchanged `coordinator::motor::tests::crash_and_stalled_control_never_allow_replacement_or_false_cleanup`. It timed out waiting for `OptionalMotor::reaped` at `motor/tests.rs:645` through the line-441 wait assertion. The failed crash/hang iteration was not recorded; no cause is inferred. **The exact same compiled test passed once alone: 1 / 0 / 0**, 5.000996141 seconds. Its source matches integration; its binary SHA-256 was identical before the full run and before/after isolation. [Both raw runs and identities](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/full-host-1337/README.md) are retained. This meets [First's explicit untouched-test handoff condition](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/issues/709#issuecomment-6176285386), tracked by Fourth in #739. **The complete host gate remains failed.** No fixture, assertion or deadline was changed for this result.

Native ARM64 run [38633124293](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38633124293) passed on exact head `d794cf2aca8fd5a7891af6363f2155e9fd3091fe`: **4,365 passed / 0 failed / 34 ignored**, 282 harnesses, GitHub Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64, Rust 1.96.0. Commands: `cargo build --locked --release --workspace --bins --examples`, then `cargo test --locked --release --workspace -- --test-threads=1`. Artifact: `lampos-arm64-d794cf2aca8fd5a7891af6363f2155e9fd3091fe`. [Terminal output and every binary checksum](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/native-d794cf/README.md). Four inherited Controls/Expression `replay_cost` filename warnings remain recorded; no warning-free workspace claim is made.

| Installable Task 31 binary | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `lamp-actions` | `33a16f446b32697b608d6ab5307ebd4917b32265635800266240b3be541dc6cb` |
| `lamp-schedule` | `12598462e7005ecbef98838dde2a83cf9c6e557de204b3a1e1d0749c90290664` |
| `lamp-voice` | `a29fcf3986cc58cd52c9142a39a280d4ae2dce62d41d8c7c999b9760a448d19f` |

The consumer durably correlates `(store_id, id, delivery)`, revalidates bounded offers, and waits for local silence, current privacy/readiness and owed camera/Second Look work. Unknown, Busy and Quiet all permit a requested reminder at that silence, as settled in the issue. Ack follows successful provider completion and final retirement of every audio generation. Interrupted or uncertain attempts remain pending without automatic re-speech. A due request cannot execute a tool or enter automatic Memory journalling, including Days mode. Schedule mutation failures and uncertain replies remain truthful.

Integration advanced during qualification from this task's `1337e7e1d8` base to `f2261ec48`. The incoming Update crate, lamp-owned unit snapshot and Memory doc change do not change affected-package/Bus/Msgs source. [Read-only integration review and clean merge preview](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/506e9e519883191dda8db565e2e3e5283c635331/lampOS/docs/verification/schedule-voice-qualification-20261015/integration-1337/incoming-update-review.md) found no new reminder conflict. The qualified artifact does not include or qualify the incoming Update crate or combined tree. **Install only Actions, Schedule and Voice; preserve installed Update and current lamp-owned unit settings, especially `LAMP_MEMORY_DAYS=on`.** Repoint executable paths and apply Schedule drop-ins; do not copy the older task-head Voice service over the current unit. Reminder-owned states and transcripts remain visible to Update's observational quiet gate.

[First's lamp qualification](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/d794cf2aca8fd5a7891af6363f2155e9fd3091fe/lampOS/docs/schedule.md#task-31-lamp-qualification) gives the off-state minute, exact service settings and disable sequence, scheduling checks and seven spoken cases. Most likely wrong on the lamp: provider schema/wording, local-silence timing in a busy office, ALSA final retirement, flash stalls and the consumer's RR20-to-Other/nice-19 transition. No lamp or real provider was accessed; host process durations and IPC probes are not acoustic or lamp latency.

pr-748.body:
Closes #709

Kind: off unless set. This is First's requested follow-up to merged #747. On lamp-4ace, First reported that “remind me in two minutes” selected a rounded `set_reminder` clock time and spoke about 73 seconds later. The two enabled catalog descriptions now direct relative durations to `set_timer` with the requested label and whole seconds, and reserve `set_reminder` for a requested clock time. Schemas, validation, clocks, deadlines and production Voice code are unchanged.

The existing switches remain exact-on: `LAMP_SCHEDULE_TOOLS=on` in Actions and Voice, with Voice delivery independently gated by `LAMP_SCHEDULE_SPEAK=on`. Two independent source copies passed 72 absent/nonenabling-switch cases and 144 exact public-catalog/Voice-helper output comparisons. This covers the disabled catalog, declarations, existing routing and ordinary Written serialization. It does not assert model choice or elapsed delivery.

Verification: [focused host evidence](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/365e36dbcd78ff247adf30b2d18afd4d9d6f1065/lampOS/docs/verification/relative-reminders-host-20261015/README.md) and [complete qualification record](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/412a46e571f38d7b8e5bd35fa5f4677fb22af650/lampOS/docs/verification/relative-reminders-qualification-20261015/README.md). The new regression reads Actions' published `tools.json`. It passes with the new descriptions and fails at the intended missing-guidance assertion against the old catalog with only the test added. That expected negative control (Cargo 101, 0 passed / 1 failed) is retained separately from positive gates.

On Third's Intel i7-10700K x86_64 Mac, macOS 26.6.2 / Darwin 25.6.0, Rust/Cargo 1.96.0:

- `cargo fmt --all --check`: passed.
- `cargo clippy --offline --locked -p lamp-actions -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Focused catalog / Voice tools: 19 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored.
- `cargo build --offline --locked --workspace`: passed, also in an independent source copy.
- Independent-copy Actions / Voice tools: 54 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored, plus the 144 byte comparisons above.
- Complete serial affected-package host gate: **FAILED: 1,604 passed / 2 failed / 13 ignored**, 65 harnesses, Cargo 101, 1,688.814767791 seconds. Command: `cargo test --offline --locked -p lamp-actions -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1`.

**Ready for lamp-voice: no. This PR is a draft.** Two unchanged motor fixtures failed at `motor/tests.rs:441`, `owned child timed out: None`. `crash_and_stalled_control_never_allow_replacement_or_false_cleanup` failed its reap wait at 645 (crash/hang iteration not recorded), then **failed once alone: 0 / 1 / 0**, 4.124137126 seconds. `late_started_callback_cannot_restore_an_offer_after_owner_replacement` failed its initial Ready wait at 865, then passed once alone: 1 / 0 / 0, 3.102594479 seconds. Both isolated invocations used the exact original compiled binary, SHA-256 `2baf1c79df5796b498857231db44e5ae5c4627d84b5f80f02b71ee7985f63117`, unchanged before/after; no rebuild or fixture/assertion/deadline edit occurred. [All original outputs and identities](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/412a46e571f38d7b8e5bd35fa5f4677fb22af650/lampOS/docs/verification/relative-reminders-qualification-20261015/full-host-365e36/README.md) are retained. [First's existing condition](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/issues/709#issuecomment-6176285386) requires an isolated pass and is **not met**. Fourth owns the repair under #739; its V6 qualification is running, with no ready PR at the dependency check. No failure cause or passing complete Mac gate is claimed.

Native ARM64 run [38644608947](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/actions/runs/38644608947) passed on exact head `365e36dbcd78ff247adf30b2d18afd4d9d6f1065`: **4,410 passed / 0 failed / 35 inherited ignored**, across 286 harnesses. Four inherited Controls/Expression `replay_cost` filename-collision warnings are retained; no warning-free workspace claim is made. The workflow runs the release workspace build and serial release workspace tests on Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 with Rust 1.96.0; its artifact targets the lamps' glibc compatibility.

Once qualified, First installs only this run's `lamp-actions` binary, SHA-256 `2c4aad6713b74ccccf55e5c2b6138f88ec8af9b5dc8d898b34138c320e6e4588`. Preserve the current lamp-owned units, character, Schedule store and Voice delivery ledger; no replacement Voice binary is required. Follow the [relative-time lamp runbook](https://github.com/autonomous-ai/lampOS/blob/365e36dbcd78ff247adf30b2d18afd4d9d6f1065/lampOS/docs/schedule.md#relative-time-follow-up-on-the-lamp): the existing off minute, then restore enabled settings and restart Actions before Voice so the next provider session reads the new catalog. Away from a minute boundary, verify one- and two-minute relative requests select 60/120-second timers with labels and never speak before their accepted elapsed deadlines; record confirmation and due audio times. Verify/list/cancel ten-minute and one-hour arguments, plus an absolute “at nine tomorrow morning” reminder. Check normal timer/light/volume/interruption/privacy behavior.

The most likely remaining gap is the live model choosing the wrong tool despite the descriptions. Host catalog tests cannot prove live selection or acoustic timing. The change adds no I/O or timer work; the existing healthy local tool-call target is 250 ms, not a measured guarantee. Third made no live-provider or lamp call.

issue-739.body:
**Why.** Speed: every builder's gate runs the whole `lamp-voice` suite, and on a loaded host one timed test fails in almost every full run, a different one each time, each passing alone. Each such failure costs a rerun and a paragraph of explanation (the fourth builder's #698 comments of 2026-10-14; the first builder's runs of 2026-10-15). On the office Mac (x86_64, load average 6 to 7 with the other builders' sessions and a podman ARM64 build), serial (`--test-threads=1`), in three full runs:

| Run (2026-10-15) | Failed | Message | Alone |
|---|---|---|---|
